title: onUninstall 'archive' with no retentionDays — a bounded hold that never says what its bound is
coversRequirement: ADR 0011 clause 1 — retentionDays is REQUIRED under 'archive'
why: 'archive' promises the tenant that its data is held for a while and then disposed of. Without retentionDays the promise has no end, so the uninstall screen states a disposal that no one can date, and the tenant cannot tell whether it has a week or a decade. The App must FAIL VALIDATION rather than install. It must specifically NOT be accepted and then given a default at install time: a default here would silently choose a disposal date for another company's data, and the App author would never see the number they are held to. Failing closed leaves the choice with the only party entitled to make it — the author who is making the promise.
notes: MUST BE REJECTED. Report side by side with adr0011-p2: rejecting both means the validator bans 'archive' outright rather than requiring the bound, and accepting both means clause 1 is unimplemented. Watch specifically for an implementation that accepts this and materialises a default retentionDays — that reads as a pass on any check that only asks 'did it install', and it is the failure mode this case exists to catch, so a runner must compare the ACCEPT/REJECT outcome and not merely the absence of an error. Decidable by the schema alone. Declares no Action at scope 'own', so no rejection here is attributable to VAL-OWN or AZ7, and it is byte-identical to adr0011-p2 apart from the lifecycle block.
